facts.statement: The genus name Tarchia means "brainy one" because researchers originally thought its brain was larger than that of Saichania.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Mongolian тархи (tarkhi, "brain") and Latin ~ia, in reference to a brain size presumed larger than that of the related form Saichania.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tarchia was found in the Barun Goyot Formation of the Nemegt Basin in Mongolia.
facts.quote: The holotype, ZPal MgD-I/111, was discovered in the Upper Cretaceous (possibly Campanian-Maastrichtian) Barun Goyot Formation (previously known as the 'Lower Nemegt Beds') of the Nemegt Basin of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Tarchia is the geologically youngest known Asian ankylosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Tarchia is the geologically youngest of all known Asian ankylosaurid dinosaurs.

facts.statement: A 2016 study by Penkalski and Tumanova identified a new species, Tarchia teresae, based on specimen PIN 3142/250.
facts.quote: In 2016, a study conducted by Paul Penkalski and Tatiana Tumanova indicated that PIN 3142/250 is not referable to Saichania due to significant anatomical differences, but instead represents a new species of Tarchia, T. teresae.

facts.statement: Jin-Young Park and colleagues named the new species Tarchia tumanovae in 2021.
facts.quote: In 2021, Jin-Young Park and team named a new species of Tarchia, T. tumanovae, known from the holotype MPC-D 100/1353 which consists of a partial skeleton with associated skull.

facts.statement: Tarchia was a medium-sized ankylosaur measuring approximately 5.5 to 6 meters long and weighing up to 2.5 to 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: Tarchia was a medium-sized ankylosaur, measuring around 5.5 - 6 m long and weighing up to 2.5 - 3 MT.

facts.statement: Tarchia had a broad, low-slung body supported by strong, short legs.
facts.quote: As an ankylosaurid, Tarchia would have had a broad, low-slung body, positioned on strong short legs.

facts.statement: Tarchia's body was protected by skin ossifications known as osteoderms.
facts.quote: The body would have been protected by skin ossifications, named osteoderms.

facts.statement: Tarchia likely possessed a bony tail club used for active defense against predators.
facts.quote: It probably had a bony tail club, for active defence against predators.

facts.statement: Researcher Arbour noted that Tarchia has a visible back of the head in top view and a deep groove surrounding an accessory osteoderm on the front of the squamosal horn.
facts.quote: In 2014, Arbour reported two distinguishing traits apart from those known exclusively from the holotype of Minotaurasaurus; the back of the head is visible in top view; and a deep groove runs along the front and outer side of the squamosal horn, and at the front it surrounds around an accessory osteoderm placed on the rear supraorbital, forming a deep furrow.

facts.statement: Tarchia teresae is distinguished from Tarchia kielanae by an unfused accessory osteoderm, unfused quadrate and paroccipital process, a sculptured skull roof, and bifurcated cranial nerve openings.
facts.quote: The study additionally found that PIN 3142/250 (i.e. T. teresae) can be distinguished from T. kielanae in that the accessory osteoderm is not fused to the roof of the skull, the quadrate and paroccipital process are not fused, the back of the skull roof is strongly sculptured, and the openings for the fourth to twelfth cranial nerves is bifurcated.

facts.statement: Tarchia lived during the Late Cretaceous period in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Tarchia (meaning "brainy one") is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Tarchia fossils were found in rocks representing eolian dunes, interdune environments, small intermittent lakes, and seasonal streams.
facts.quote: The rocks in which Tarchia fossils were found likely represent eolian dunes and interdune environments, with small intermittent lakes and seasonal streams.

facts.statement: Tarchia was a herbivore that fed as a low-level bulk feeder using its broad, sub-rectangular muzzle.
facts.quote: Tarchia was, like other Mongolian ankylosaurines, herbivorous and a low-level bulk feeder based on its sub-rectangular broad muzzle.

facts.statement: Living in dry environments, Tarchia may have relied on hindgut fermentation or consumed succulent plants rather than complex chewing.
facts.quote: Instead of oral processing, ankylosaurids living in dry environments such as Tarchia may have relied more on hindgut fermentation for digestion or, alternatively, consumed succulent plants that did not require complex chewing.

facts.statement: A Tarchia skull bears tooth marks from the tyrannosaurid Tarbosaurus, providing evidence that this theropod hunted the ankylosaurid.
facts.quote: One skull of Tarchia shows tooth marks identified as belonging to the tyrannosaurid, Tarbosaurus, indicating the theropod hunted the ankylosaurid.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Dyoplosaurus giganteus is a valid species or a nomen dubium, leading some researchers to revive the name Tarchia kielanae.
facts.quote: However, recent study by Victoria Megan Arbour indicates that D. giganteus is indistinguishable from other ankylosaurs from the late Campanian-Maastrichtian of Mongolia, and hence a nomen dubium; the study revived the name Tarchia kielanae.

facts.statement: Researcher Arbour concluded that Minotaurasaurus is a junior synonym of Tarchia based on shared distinguishing traits.
facts.quote: Arbour discovered that the holotype of Tarchia shared distinguishing traits with that of Minotaurasaurus Miles & Miles 2009, concluding that the latter is a junior synonym of Tarchia.

facts.quote: En 1970, en Mongolia, una expedición polaco-mongola descubrió un cráneo de anquilosáurido cerca de Khulsan

facts.statement: Teresa Maryańska named and described the type species Tarchia kielanae in 1977.
facts.quote: En 1977, Teresa Maryańska nombró y describió la especie tipo Tarchia kielanae

facts.statement: The generic name Tarchia derives from the Mongolian word 'tarkhi' meaning 'brain' and Latin '-ia', referencing a supposedly larger brain size than the related Saichania.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del mongol tarkhi, "cerebro" y del latín ~ia , en referencia a un tamaño de cerebro supuestamente mayor que el de la forma relacionada Saichania

facts.statement: The specific name honors Professor Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska, the leader of the expedition.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a la profesora Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska, líder de la expedición

facts.statement: The holotype ZPAL MgD-I/111 was discovered in the Upper Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation.
facts.quote: El holotipo, ZPal MgD-I/111, fue descubierto en la Formación Barun Goyot del Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Maryańska referred three additional specimens: ZPAL MgDI/43 (a large postcranial skeleton with three 'free' tail vertebrae, twelve fused 'club' tail vertebrae, and a shield), ZPAL MgDI/49 (right humerus), and PIN 3142/251 (a skeleton with skull still undescribed).
facts.quote: Maryańska refirió tres especímenes adicionales, ZPAL MgDI/43, un gran esqueleto poscraneal que contiene tres vértebras de la cola "libres", doce vértebras fusionadas de la cola del "mango" del garrote de la cola y un escudo, ZPAL MgDI/49, húmero derecho y PIN 3142/251, un esqueleto con cráneo, que aún permanece sin describir

facts.statement: In 1977, Tatyana Tumanova named a second species, Tarchia gigantea.
facts.quote: En 1977, Tatyana Tumanova nombró una segunda especie, Tarchia gigantea

facts.statement: This was a name change from Dyoplosaurus giganteus Maleev 1956, based on specimen PIN 551/29.
facts.quote: Este fue un cambio de nombre de Dyoplosaurus giganteus Maleev 1956, que se había basado en el espécimen PIN 551/29

facts.statement: In 1987, Tumanova concluded both species were identical, making Dyoplosaurus giganteus the primary synonym and renaming the species Tarchia gigantea.
facts.quote: En 1987, Tumanova concluyó que ambas especies eran idénticas, esto haría de Dyoplosaurus giganteus el sinónimo primario sobre Tarchia kielanae y la especie cambiaria de nombre a Tarchia gigantea

facts.statement: A recent study by Victoria Megan Arbor indicates D. giganteus is indistinguishable from other late Campanian to Maastrichtian Mongolian ankylosaurids, making it a dubious name, and the study revived the name Tarchia kielanae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio reciente de Victoria Megan Arbor indica que D. giganteus es indistinguible de otros anquilosáuridos del Campaniano tardío a Maastrichtiense de Mongolia y, por lo tanto, una denominación dudosa y el estudio revivió el nombre de Tarchia kielanae

facts.statement: In 2016, a study by Penkalski & Tumanova indicated that PIN 3142/250 represents a new Tarchia species, Tarchia teresae, due to significant anatomical differences from Saichania.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, en 2016, un estudio realizado por Penkalski & Tumanova indicó que PIN 3142/250 no se puede referir a Saichania debido a diferencias anatómicas significativas, sino que representa una nueva especie de Tarchia, Tarchia teresae

facts.statement: In 2021, Jin-Young Park and colleagues named a new species, Tarchia tumanovae, known from holotype MPC-D 100/1353, a partial skeleton with an associated skull.
facts.quote: En 2021, Jin-Young Park y su equipo nombraron una nueva especie, Tarchia tumanovae, conocida por el holotipo MPC-D 100/1353 que consiste en un esqueleto parcial con un cráneo asociado

facts.statement: It was found in the Nemegt Formation at the Hermiin Tsav locality.
facts.quote: Se encontró en la Formación Nemegt en la localidad de Hermiin Tsav

facts.statement: In 2021, Park, J.Y. and colleagues described a specimen from the Nemegt Formation, Mongolia, as a new species, T. tumanovae.
facts.quote: En 2021, Park, J.Y. y colegas encontraron un espécimen perteneciente al género en la Formación Nemegt, también en Mongolia, que fue descrito como una nueva especie, T. tumanovae

facts.statement: Arbor's study concluded that specimen PIN 3142/250, referred to Tarchia in 1977 by Tumanova, likely belonged to Saichania.
facts.quote: El estudio de Arbor también concluyó que el espécimen PIN 3142/250, referido en 1977 a Tarchia por Tumanova, probablemente pertenecía a Saichania

facts.statement: This would radically change the common image of Tarchia, as this specimen had been the best preserved and the basis for most illustrations, museum mounts, and scientific research.
facts.quote: Esto cambiaría radicalmente la imagen común de Tarchia ya que este ejemplar había sido, con mucho, el mejor conservado y la mayoría de las ilustraciones, los montajes de museos y, de hecho, la investigación científica se habían basado en él

facts.statement: Tarchia was previously distinguished from Saichania based on a relatively larger basicranium, an unfused paroccipital process, contact with the quadrate, and, according to PIN 3142/250, a premaxillary shelf wider than the maximum distance between tooth rows in the maxillae.
facts.quote: Tarchia se había distinguido previamente de Saichania sobre la base de su basicráneo relativamente más grande, un proceso paroccipital no fusionado, el contacto con el cuadrado y, según PIN 3142/250, el hecho de que la tribuna premaxilar es más ancha que la distancia máxima entre las filas de dientes en los maxilares

facts.statement: In 2014, Arbor reported two additional distinctive traits besides those known exclusively from the Minotaurasaurus holotype: the back of the head is visible from above, and a deep groove runs across the front and outer side of the squamosal horn, surrounding an accessory osteoderm placed on the posterior supraorbital, forming a deep groove.
facts.quote: En 2014, Arbor informó de otors dos rasgos distintivos además de los conocidos exclusivamente del holotipo de Minotaurasaurus: la parte posterior de la cabeza es visible en la vista superior; y un surco profundo recorre el frente y el lado externo del cuerno escamoso, y en el frente rodea un osteodermo accesorio colocado en el supraorbitario posterior, formando un surco profundo

facts.statement: The 2016 redescription of Tarchia notes it differs from Saichania by having a postorbital fossa separating the squamosal horn from the supraorbital and an accessory osteoderm, a visible occiput in dorsal view, a large and deep skull, a foramen magnum taller than wide, and nuchal osteoderms taller laterally than medially.
facts.quote: La redescripción de 2016 de Tarchia señala que se diferencia de Saichania en que tiene una fosa postorbitaria, que separa el cuerno escamoso del supraorbitario y un osteodermo accesorio, siendo visible el occipucio en vista dorsal, el cráneo grande y profundo, el foramen magnum es más alto que ancho y los osteodermos nucales son más altos lateralmente que medialmente

facts.statement: Additionally, it differs from both Saichania and Minotaurasaurus by lacking postocular caputegulae, or small polygonal bony plates behind the orbit, and having a proportionally high occiput in caudal view.
facts.quote: Además, se diferencia tanto de Saichania como de Minotaurasaurus en que carece de caputegulas postoculares, o pequeñas placas óseas poligonales detrás de la órbita y tiene un occipucio proporcionalmente alto en vista caudal

facts.statement: The study found that PIN 3142/250, i.e., T. teresae, can be distinguished from T. kielanae because the accessory osteoderm is not fused to the skull roof, the quadrate and paroccipital process are not fused, the back of the skull roof is strongly sculpted, and openings for cranial nerves four to twelve are bifurcated.
facts.quote: El estudio también encontró que el PIN 3142/250, es decir, T. teresae, se puede distinguir de T. kielanae en que el osteodermo accesorio no está fusionado con el techo del cráneo, el cuadrado y el proceso paroccipital no están fusionados, la parte posterior del techo del cráneo está fuertemente esculpida y las aberturas para los nervios craneales cuarto a duodécimo están bifurcadas

facts.statement: Much of the information provided about Tarchia in previous works refers to PIN 3142/250, which was briefly referred to Saichania until it was named T. teresae in 2016.
facts.quote: Gran parte de la información proporcionada sobre Tarchia en trabajos anteriores se refiere al PIN 3142/250, que se refirió brevemente a Saichania hasta que se denominó T. teresae en 2016

facts.statement: In 2001, it was claimed that wear facets indicative of tooth-to-tooth occlusion are present in Tarchia, which likely does not refer to the holotype, as teeth are not preserved in the holotype.
facts.quote: En 2001, se afirmó que, en Tarchia, están presentes facetas de desgaste indicativas de oclusión de diente a diente, lo que probablemente no se refiere al espécimen holotipo, ya que en el holotipo no se conservan dientes
